# Terminal upgrades for DeepSeek Harness
Terminal upgrades for DeepSeek Harness. The first one: hold **Option** over a URL in a terminal and
it underlines; click it and it opens in your browser. The trigger key is configurable.
## Features
- **The link underlines while you hold the trigger key.** The underline is drawn over the URL's cell
s in the URL's own color, and the pointer becomes a hand, so you can see what is clickable before yo

u click.
- **Click opens the browser.** Clicking `http://localhost:3000` from `next dev` opens it in

a new tab; the desktop app hands the URL to your default browser.
- **Configurable trigger key.** O

ption by default; Command or Control from the plugin config.
- **Plain clicks are untouched.** Text
selection, double-click word selection, and keystrokes reach the terminal exactly as before. Only th

e trigger key on a link is intercepted.
- **No terminal changes.** The plugin reads the rows the ter
minal already renders and adds its own overlay; it never rewrites terminal text, so output, colors,

and the shell are unaffected.
- **Works with every terminal tab**, including ones opened after insta
lling, and disposes cleanly when the plugin is removed.
## Install
In the desktop app, open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Add plugin**, and enter this directory
. The desktop profile is managed by the Electron app, which is why this is the preferred path there.
For another profile, use the CLI:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Replace `<profile>` with the name shown by `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` (for example `web`).
Restart the Host or reload the page after installing.
The package ships its browser bundle (`client.js`), so no build step is required to install it.
## Usage

1. Run something that prints a URL, for example `pnpm dev` in a Next.js project.
2. Hold the trigger
key — **Option** (`⌥`) by default — and move the pointer over the URL. The URL underlines and the t
erminal cursor becomes a hand. Pressing the key while already resting on a link underlines it withou

t moving the pointer.
3. Click. The URL opens in a new browser tab. In the desktop app it opens in t

er.
3. Click. The URL opens in a new browser tab. In the desktop app it opens in the system browser.
Without the trigger key, clicking the same URL does what it always did: it places the terminal curso
r and starts a text selection.
## Configuration
The trigger key defaults to **Option** (Alt). Change it in the plugin's profile entry config:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| `triggerKey` | Key |

| `alt` (default) | Option on macOS, Alt on Windows and Linux |
| `meta` | Command |
| `ctrl` | Cont

t` (default) | Option on macOS, Alt on Windows and Linux |
| `meta` | Command |
| `ctrl` | Control |
Restart DeepSeek Harness after changing it: the profile applies plugin config at startup. The Host v
alidates the value while it starts, so an unknown key stops the plugin with an explicit error instea
d of silently falling back. The browser reads the setting once as the page loads and keeps Option un
til the answer arrives.
Only the configured key triggers the underline and the click; the other modifiers stay inert, so not
hing changes for people who use them for other terminal gestures.
## How it works
DeepSeek Harness renders terminals with xterm's DOM renderer, so the visible rows exist as text in t
he page. The plugin listens on `document`, maps a pointer position to the terminal row and character
offset, and runs the same URL rules for any row under the pointer:

- `http://` and `https://` only.
- Sentence punctuation after a URL and an unbalanced closing bracke

t are left out, so `see https://example.test/docs.` links the URL without the period.
- A balanced c
loser stays part of the link, so `https://example.test/a_(b)` keeps its `)`.
Client plugins do not receive profile entry config, so the Host half validates `triggerKey` and publ
ishes it on one loopback route, `/__dsh/terminal-upgrades`; the browser reads it once at startup. Th
e underline itself is an overlay element the plugin owns, positioned from the URL's text runs, so th
e terminal's own DOM is never modified.
The plugin adds no slot, no terminal state, and no per-terminal setup, so it has nothing to clean up
beyond removing its listeners and its overlay.
## Limitations
- **One row at a time.** A URL that wraps onto the next terminal row is not detected; short links su

ch as `http://localhost:3000` are unaffected.
- **Underline is an overlay.** It tracks the text runs
the terminal rendered. Scrolling hides it until the pointer moves again, and a very unusual font fa

llback could shift it by a pixel.
- **Programs that capture the mouse.** In a terminal program that
reports mouse clicks itself, such as Vim or `less`, a trigger-keyed click on a link is consumed by t

he plugin; a trigger-keyed click elsewhere still reaches the program.
- **DOM renderer only.** The d
etection reads the rendered rows. If the terminal switches to a canvas or WebGL renderer, nothing is

detected and the plugin does nothing.
- **Not a general link opener.** File paths, line numbers, an
d bare host names are not links.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`src/client.js` is the browser source, `index.js` is the Host half, and `scripts/build-client.mjs` b
undles the browser half into `client.js` wrapped in the Harness module-loader shape. Edit `src/`, ru
n `pnpm run build`, and reload the page.
